text:
maya: ran an nsys trace against the staging workload that regressed yesterday, dropping p99 by ~30ms. attaching quick notes + a perfetto link :eyes:

alex: thanks — can you paste the top kernel table?

maya: sure, snippet from `nsys stats` on the trace:
```
Top kernels by GPU time (ns):
  matmul_32x32_kernel        1.24s  (45.6%)
  attention_fwd_kernel       0.42s  (15.4%)
  kv_lookup_kernel           0.28s   (10.3%)
  layernorm_fwd              0.18s   (6.6%)
  softmax_block              0.14s   (5.1%)
  misc_memcopy               0.12s   (4.4%)
```
This is the bad run. baseline traces last week had matmul at ~28% not 45%.

rachel: wow matmul jumped a lot. did you change compiler flags or kernel selection heuristics in the batching PR?

maya: yeah the batching change toggled a different GEMM variant for small batch sizes (we moved to the fused 32x32 kernel to improve latency for tiny batches). I suspected it would help but the profile shows it spends more time overall now due to reduced occupancy and more warp stalls.

samir: can you share the occupancy / SM util numbers?

maya: copied from Nsight summary (same trace):
```
matmul_32x32_kernel:  SM Util 37%   Avg Active Warps 14.2  (low occupancy)
attention_fwd_kernel:   SM Util 78%   Avg Active Warps 28.1
kv_lookup_kernel:       SM Util 19%   High L2 misses, serial warps
```
So the new matmul variant has poor SM utilization at 1-2 tokens per batch path. We earlier thought its lower latency per-invocation would win but it harms throughput when theres more concurrency.

alex: interesting — do we have a comparison of measured latency per token vs per-request? maybe the per-request latency looked slightly better, but the overall token throughput regressed.

maya: yes. quick numbers from perf harness:
- baseline (old kernel): avg token latency 1.8ms, p99 12ms, token/sec 225k
- new kernel (this PR): avg token latency 1.6ms, p99 42ms, token/sec 168k

rachel: p99 went up a lot — looks like tail amplification from queuing. Could be the kernel's launch overhead + serial execution on some SMs causing head-of-line blocking.

samir: any strange host-side CPU spikes?

maya: CPU flat, but I see a repeated pattern in perfetto timeline: matmul kernels launch in short bursts separated by long gaps while other kernels (attention_fwd) cram into a few SMs. link: https://perfetto.link/trace/abcd1234 (redwood-internal)

perf-bot: automated diff for 1832501200: changed kernel_selector.go: preferFusedGEMM for batch_size <= 4 -> true  :warning:

alex: ok root cause hypothesis: the selector flips to fused 32x32 for small batches, that kernel has poor occupancy for our model shapes; under mixed workload it causes SM fragmentation and queuing.

rachel: mitigation ideas:
- revert selector toggle for now (safe rollback)
- implement a micro-benchmark at startup to choose GEMM variant per-device based on measured occupancy/latency
- add runtime sampling to switch kernel variant when throughput drops

maya: I prototyped the micro-bench (30s run) and it correctly picks the high-occupancy kernel on our test instance. patch WIP.

samir: one more ask — can you produce a minimal repro with nsys + NVTX ranges so we can correlate host-side queuing with kernel launches? put it in a short CI job.

maya: yup on it. I'll add a small harness that runs the same request mix we saw and emits NVTX ranges around batching and cache lookup. planning to open a PR with trace + revert in the next 4 hours.

alex: awesome. if possible include an annotation in the trace showing per-kernel shared memory & register usage (those are suspects for low active warps).

maya: will do. filing the issue: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RINF-2917

rachel: thanks maya — once we have the micro-bench result we can auto-gate the kernel selector change behind a perf test. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: note: alert if p99 token latency > 30ms for two consecutive CI runs on staging.

maya: closing loop here once PR is up, ping me if you want the raw trace.
